findings.reason: Inspected the exact 菜 entry on printed p. 49 (PDF p. 61). Its component sequence identifies the Shuowen seal form and later Han and regular-script forms, but the individual glyph specimens g023–g026 are not all independently identifiable at this scan resolution, so their identities remain unresolved. No claim in the supplied 菜 article depends on identifying those specimens: its structural analysis is independently supported by E3 and X-e928d816cc35ad00c241; its book-backed definition and cited usage by X-4497e60de71980f3e5c6; and the historical-form inventory and its limits by X-84480be72ab756756291 and X-eab6061234892b217094. The article does not claim dates or identities for the individual book specimens. The scan itself confirms printed page 49, so null printed-page metadata is an omission, not an unresolved page-number reading.
